description.short: One of the most balanced and accessible Dan Cong aroma types, with a honey-fruity bouquet
description.overview: Named after the Daoist legend of the Eight Immortals, reflecting this tea's status as one of the classic, revered Dan Cong varieties.
description.aroma: Honey and fruit, with delicate floral undertones
description.taste: Balanced and gently sweet, with a full body and smooth minerality
description.processing: Classic Dan Cong craft: withering → shaking → kill-green → rolling → baking/roasting

history.origin: The name alludes to the Daoist 'Eight Immortals' — a beloved motif in Chinese mythology representing diverse paths to perfection.
history.development: Considered one of the venerable, well-established Fenghuang aroma cultivars cultivated across multiple plots on the mountain.
history.modern: One of the more widely produced Dan Cong teas, making it more accessible in price compared to single-tree micro-lots.
interestingFacts: Unlike some Dan Congs harvested strictly from a single ancient mother tree, Ba Xian is frequently propagated and produced from clonal bushes of that lineage, ensuring consistent flavor from batch to batch.
